A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VQToken study, with matching methods, equations, six tables and three figures. All 11 pages were inspected; neither PDF contains an appendix. V5 clips some introduction text on page 2, but that text remains extractable, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original VQToken benchmark results, token-compression and efficiency measurements, component ablations and clustering visualizations in Tables 1–6 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: V5 retains the original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations and visualizations reported in v4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same fixed/adaptive K-Means clustering, centroid codebook, spatial–temporal index map and VQ-Attention mechanism. No algorithm, architecture or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Evaluation still covers ActivityNet-QA, VideoMME, NExT-QA, LongVideoBench and MVBench. V5 names LLaVA-Video-178K as the source of the already-described 178K training videos and 1.3M instruction samples; this clarifies provenance rather than establishing changed coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including Token Pruning, ToMe, VidToMe, interpolation, DyCoke and the video-language model baselines. The Segment Anything clustering comparison is also retained.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the 0.5B backbone, 85,000 training iterations, stated training hyperparameters, fixed token budgets of 12/32/64, adaptive evaluation settings and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The component and randomization ablations in Table 6, MVBench subtask analysis in Figure 3, and adaptive K-Means versus Segment Anything visualization in Figure 2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their numerical entries, and Figures 2–3 retain their visual findings. For example, Table 3 reports dynamic VQToken accuracy of 57.72 with 13.08 average tokens and fixed VQToken accuracy of 57.46 with 32 tokens in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the reduction-task and TokDense definitions, and the module/LLM complexity expressions are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same novelty, compression and performance claims, including 0.07% token retention with a claimed 0.66% NextQA-MC accuracy drop. Adding VQToken to the title does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of positional preservation, VQ-Attention's contribution and K-Means efficiency relative to Segment Anything are retained. The computational-resource constraint and future-work directions also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V5 replaces the promise of releasing code and models upon acceptance with project, GitHub code and Hugging Face model links. Section 4.1.1 also explicitly names LLaVA-Video-178K. These add access information and data provenance; the PDFs do not establish the external resources' availability or contents.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the claimed relationship to prior token-reduction methods. The new NeurIPS 2025 footer is publication metadata.

P1.justification: V5 prefixes the title with VQToken, adds SMILE Lab affiliations, updates correspondence and publication text, and clarifies the training-data source. Section ordering and the scientific narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised title and resource-link block reflow the opening pages. V5 also introduces a large gap on page 2 that pushes several introduction lines below the page boundary; v4 displays them normally. The six tables and three figures retain their content and arrangement.

improvement.justification: V5 improves documented resource access and training-data provenance, but introduces a confirmed page-2 layout defect that hides part of the introduction during normal viewing. The scientific evidence is unchanged. The local PDFs do not establish a reliable net direction between these gains and the readability loss, particularly because the linked resources cannot be assessed.
